captions.instagram:
How does 2D animation work?

Every cartoon is a pile of drawings. Flip a flip-book, fill in a jump between key poses, switch the 12 principles on and off on a bouncing ball, spread cels out under a multiplane camera, and make a mango-headed kid talk.

→ A 2D cartoon is a flip-book made big: many drawings, each a little different.
→ On twos, each drawing is shown twice: 12 drawings for 24 frames a second.
→ The key animator draws three poses: the crouch, the top of the jump and the landing.
→ In-betweeners fill the gaps, bunching drawings near the top so the jump slows like gravity.
→ Squash, stretch, slow in and out, and arcs turn a circle into a bouncing ball.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/anim2dclear (link in bio)

Box No. 058 of 365. Follow @glassbox.how for a new "how it works" every day.

youtubeLong.title: How does 2D animation work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Every cartoon is a pile of drawings. Flip a flip-book, fill in a jump between key poses, switch the 12 principles on and off on a bouncing ball, spread cels out under a multiplane camera, and make a mango-headed kid talk.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/anim2dclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/anim2dclear

In this video:
• A flip-book made big. A cartoon is thousands of still drawings, each a little different, shown one after another.
• Keys first, in-betweens after. The key animator draws the poses that tell the story.
• Twelve principles. Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston’s The Illusion of Life (1981) lists the 12 principles: squash and stretch, anticipation, staging, straight ahead and pose to pose, follow-through, slow in and out, arcs, secondary action, timing, exaggeration, solid drawing and appeal.
• Cels, backgrounds and depth. From 1914, moving characters were inked and painted on clear cels over one painted background.
• Rigs, tweens and curves. On a computer, you can still draw every frame, or build a cut-out rig of pieces on pivots.
• Making drawings talk. The voice is recorded first and read frame by frame onto an exposure sheet.

Glassbox opens one box a day: an interactive model of how something works, plus the code behind it.
